title: ALMA Reveals an Inhomogeneous Compact Rotating Dense Molecular Torus at the NGC 1068 Nucleus
question: Do HCN J=3–2 and HCO+ J=3–2 trace a rotating dense molecular torus at the NGC 1068 nucleus, and what are its morphology and dynamics?

evidence.quote: the inclination angle ($i$) is estimated to be $i$ = 34–46$^{\circ}$ (cite: gar16)

what.value: SMBH mass ~1e7 Msun from water maser disk

evidence.quote: SMBH mass of NGC 1068, $\sim$ 1 $\times$ 10$^{7}$M$_{\odot}$ (cite: gre96; hur02; lod03)

recipe.method: uvcontsub then clean on continuum-subtracted data; two datasets (a) H1 only and (b) all
imfit on moment 0 maps for PA and deconvolved sizes
Spectra in 0.2x0.15 arcsec rectangle; Gaussian fits

recipe.goal: Derive dense gas mass and enclosed dynamical mass
recipe.method: L'HCN to M_dense with factor 10; Keplerian enclosed mass from v/sin i ~20 km/s at r~3 pc
assumptions: HCN optically thick and thermalized so L'(1-0)=L'(3-2); Keplerian rotation; i=34 deg

evidence.quote: 186$\pm$17 mas $\times$ 63$\pm$7 mas (13 pc $\times$ 4 pc) for HCN J=3–2
peak optical LSR velocity = 1137$\pm$3 (km s$^{-1}$), full-width at half-maximum FWHM = 156$\pm$9 (km s$^{-1}$)

not_stated_but_needed: Final beam sizes and rms noise
Which Cycle 4 execution blocks were combined in (b) and weighting between datasets
score_reason: Project codes and main imaging parameters given, but many processing details and kinematic derivation steps are sparse.
rediscovery_reason: Data from ALMA archive, imfit sizes, PAs and Gaussian fit numbers are checkable, though some settings are missing.
